old: "title": "Causality & Historical Preconditions: miatt, következtében, eredményeképpen"
new: "title": "Causes in History: miatt, ezért"
why: következtében and eredményeképpen are causal-postpositions, taught in B1 Unit 31

old: To analyze complex historical causation, Hungarian uses postpositions denoting cause: *miatt* (+ nominative: 'because of'), *következtében* (+ genitive *-nak/-nek*: 'as a consequence of'), and *eredményeképpen* ('as a result of').
new: You know *miatt* ('because of', after a noun) from A2 Unit 40 and *ezért* ('so') from A2 Unit 31. History texts use them to link causes and results: *a pénzhiány miatt* (because of the lack of money), *…, ezért …* (…, so …).
why: screen taught a B1 Unit 31 form before its unit; recap of known miatt/ezért instead

old: "english": "As a consequence of the retaliation for the 1514 peasant revolt, the serfs lost their right to free movement."
new: "english": "The reprisal for the revolt was harsh, so the serfs lost their right of free movement."

old: Narrating campaigns requires temporal conjunctions: *amikor* (when), *miután* (after + past tense), and *mielőtt* (before + conditional or past). Notice that *mielőtt* frequently takes the conditional mood (*mielőtt megérkezett volna* = before it had arrived).
new: You know *amikor* (when), *miután* (after + past tense) and *mielőtt* (before) from B1 Unit 1. Here they put the events of a campaign in order. With *mielőtt* the verb stays in the plain past: *Mielőtt a vár elesett, …* (Before the fortress fell, …).
why: recap (B1 Unit 1, miutan-mielott); the past conditional with volna is taught in B1 Unit 39

old: "english": "After Sultan Suleiman I ascended the throne, he immediately launched a campaign against Hungary."
new: "english": "After Sultan Suleiman I ascended the throne, he launched a campaign against Hungary."

old: "english": "Nándorfehérvár fell in 1521 before the royal army could have relieved it."
new: "english": "Before Nándorfehérvár fell, the Hungarian court asked for help."

old: "title": "Expressing Rapid Succession & Tactical Drama: alighogy... máris, hirtelen"
new: "title": "Describing Sudden Events: amint, rövid idő alatt, hirtelen"
why: alighogy ... máris is taught in B2 Unit (b2-14-01)

old: Military engagements that turn abruptly use correlative constructions such as *alighogy... máris* ('no sooner had... than already...'), *rövid idő alatt* ('in a short time'), and *hirtelen* ('suddenly').
new: You know *amint* ('as soon as') from B1 Unit 1. Accounts of a battle add phrases for sudden change: *rövid idő alatt* ('in a short time') and *hirtelen* ('suddenly').
why: B2 construction replaced by a recap of amint (B1 Unit 1) and the unit's own phrases

old: "english": "Hardly had the Hungarian cavalry charge begun when it already met devastating cannon fire."
new: "english": "As soon as the Hungarian cavalry charge began, it ran into devastating cannon fire."

old: "english": "Pál Tomori, archbishop of Kalocsa and commander-in-chief, fell on the battlefield fighting heroically."
new: "english": "Pál Tomori, archbishop of Kalocsa and commander-in-chief of the army, was killed in the battle."

old: "title": "Attributive & Predicative Participles in Tragedy: elmerült, megfulladt, menekülő"
new: "title": "Describing the King's Fate: elhunyt, megfulladt, menekülő"
why: the screen is a recap; "predicative" is not what it shows

old: Hungarian uses the past participle suffix *-t / -tt* and present participle *-ó / -ő* to characterize historical figures and their fates: *a megfulladt uralkodó* (the drowned monarch), *a menekülő katonák* (the fleeing soldiers).
new: You know the past participle *-t / -tt* as a modifier from B1 Unit 3 and the present participle *-ó / -ő* from B1 Unit 11. Here they describe historical figures and their fates: *a megfulladt uralkodó* (the drowned monarch), *a menekülő katonák* (the fleeing soldiers).

new: "english": "The death of the young king, who drowned in the water, caused a dynastic crisis."
